To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified a new variant of vga(A), vga(A) LC, which is a gene conferring resistance to both lncosamides and to streptogramins.

a new variant of a macrolide resistance protein, Vga(A), was identified in S. haenolyticus strains with a LSA phenotype and that the substrate specificity of the Vga(A) protein was changed by four amino acid substitutions in the spacer between two ATP-binding caskets.

the ABC protein Vga(A) from S. aureus, which is a well-known macrolide-stretogramin B transporter, has a variant, Vga(A)L, which is a lincosamide and streptogramins A transporter, and that this variant is responsible for the lincosamid and streptogramines A resistance of Staphyloccus haemolyticum.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the discovery of the first variant of the Vga(A) ABC protein, which confers resistance to lincosamids and streptogramins, and which is encoded by a new gene, vga (A) LC, and with the elucidation of the mechanism of lncosamide-stretpogramin A resistance.
a novel evolutionary variant of a streptogramin resistance protein, Vga(A), which is able to confer lincosamide and streptogramine resistance in S.
the identification of the new ABC protein Vga(A) LC and with a description of the molecular basis of the LSA phenotype, which is a new variant of streptogramin resistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ABC protein Vga(A) is the first example of a multidrug transporter that can be converted into a lincosamide-resistant enzyme by a few mutations.

the vga(A) gene family encodes proteins that confer resistance to macrolides, streptogramin B, and/or lincosamiders, and the substrate specificity of Vga(A)ABC proteins is determined by a small number of amino acids located within the linker region.

the vga(A) gene family encodes a group of ABC proteins with different antibiotic specificities and substrate specificities, depending on the species of the host and the genetic background of each strain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ABC transporter encoded by vga(A) and its variant vga(A) LC, which are the first two ABC transporters described in staphylococci, have different substrate specificities: the former is involved in macrolide-stretogramin B resistance, and the latter is involved in lincosamide and streptogramins A resistance.

the ABC protein Vga(A) was originally evolved to confer resistance to streptograms, and later, by accumulation of point mutations in the substrate-recognization site, it evolved to become an ABC protein with a new substrate spectrum that included both lincosamide and streptogramins.
the ABC protein Vga(A) is a substrate-specific protein with a broad substrate spectrum, and Vga(A)Lc is an evolutionary variant of Vga(A) that has a shifted substrate spectrum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Vga(A)-like ABC proteins can be modified to acquire new substrate specificities, and this may be a mechanism for generating resistance to new antibiotics.
the ABC protein Vga(A) is a substrate for both macrolides and lincosamids, and the substrate specificity can be shifted by amino acid substitutions.
the substrate specificity of ABC proteins can be altered by a limited number of amino acid substitutions.
